page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System and driven by custom AWS Graviton ARM64 architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU clocked at 3.3 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. Operating without simultaneous multithreading, the dedicated single-thread execution guarantees deterministic compute performance without thread contention on the physical core.

A key architectural feature of the c9gd.medium is its bundled 59 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume. This attached non-volatile storage offers low-latency block access compared to network-attached block devices, making it effective for scratch spaces, local caches, and temporary data ingestion pipelines. Networking throughput features a baseline capacity of 1 Gbps, aligning with standard small-footprint infrastructure requirements.

Resource allocation follows a strict 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio common to compute-intensive families. While the 2.0 GB RAM footprint bounds the instance from running memory-heavy application runtimes or extensive in-memory stores, it offers strong operational cost efficiency for lightweight parallel jobs. The presence of direct NVMe storage without relying strictly on remote EBS storage reduces baseline storage transfer overhead for ephemeral tasks.

The c9gd.medium is tailored for lightweight compute tasks adapted for ARM64 architectures. Typical workloads include microservices, stateless batch processors, local CI/CD testing runners, small containerized application nodes, and edge web proxy services requiring dedicated CPU cycles and fast local temporary storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.medium is a compute-optimized, single-core cloud instance powered by AWS custom ARM64 Graviton processors. Operating under the AWS Nitro System, the instance delivers 1 dedicated vCPU operating at 3.3 GHz without multithreading, alongside 2.0 GB of RAM. Designed for tasks requiring high CPU clocks and local storage speed, it includes 59 GB of bundled NVMe SSD instance storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers cost-efficient compute cycles for lightweight applications while avoiding the resource sharing common to burstable models. The integrated local NVMe drive provides fast input/output operations for scratch space and temporary caches. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, single-threaded processing workers, continuous integration steps, and caching web services optimized for ARM64 instruction sets.
